heroHeadline: Nearly Pristine Palmyra Atoll Reefs Offer a Restoration Blueprint — as California Vetoes New Plastic-Fund Spending Rules
heroSubtitle: NPR reported September 18, 2026 that Palmyra Atoll, a remote U.S. wildlife refuge in the central Pacific, still hosts some of the world's healthiest coral reefs — recovering strongly from a 2023 bleaching event even as renewed 2026 heat stress emerges — giving researchers at The Nature Conservancy, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Stanford, and the Coral Restoration Consortium a rare baseline for reef recovery. On September 19, the Center for Coastal Studies freed an entangled minke whale in Cape Cod Bay, its entanglement-response program's latest rescue since 1984. And on September 20, California Governor Gavin Newsom vetoed SB 1180, which would have set binding spending rules for the state's roughly $5 billion SB 54 Plastic Pollution Mitigation Fund, saying the bill risked complicating funding already underway.
